# Session review template

Use after processing is authorized, following the
[session analysis guide](../reference/session-analysis.md). Replace prompts with
reviewed evidence; this template is not a completed session review. The intended
output is `docs/days/day-XX/sessions/<topic>-<video-id>.md`. Keep full text in
ignored `.data/`; this artifact is a concise, nonverbatim interpretation.

## Source and review state

- Session title, event day, video ID, and canonical source URL:
- Caption/ASR input paths and SHA-256 hashes:
- Review state: not started / provisional caption-only / source-reviewed.
- Exact reviewed intervals and unreviewed gaps, in video-relative time:
- Source playback checks: intervals, reviewer, check performed, finding:
- Timing anomalies, caption limitations, and any verified full-day alignment:
- Processing authorization and privacy/publication restrictions:
- Raw evidence availability and temporary-input cleanup state:

## In brief

What problem did the session address? What did participants attempt? What is the
most useful supported takeaway? Keep this short and cite the supporting items
below. Do not present a speaker's success claim as a verified result.

## What happened

Organize by chronological topics, not caption chunks. Use one row per meaningful
exchange or action; add detail only where needed to understand what changed.

| Source interval | Participants and attribution basis | Request, action, or discussion | Evidence type and review state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Distinguish human questions, advice, observations, generated output, narrated
activity, and observed results. Separate human and bot identities, and the
speaker from the attributed author of any response being read.

## Decisions and outcomes

| Item | Evidence and interval | State | Constraints, alternatives, or unresolved verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Use precise states: proposed, requested, attempted, completion reported,
demonstrated, independently verified, blocked, or unresolved. For an accepted
decision, identify who accepted it and the evidence of acceptance. If none were
identified, say so only for the reviewed scope.

## Lessons and things to try

| Lesson or practice | Supporting interval and evidence type | Conditions, limits, or counterevidence | Proposed learning exercise and success check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Separate observed practices, participant opinions, and analyst hypotheses.
Exercises are analyst proposals unless the recording establishes otherwise;
include a safe, bounded test and an observable success criterion. Do not execute
them as part of writing this review.

## Relationship to other evidence

Link relevant session reviews or full-day chapters. Classify each comparison as
additional coverage, consistent account, contradiction, or unresolved. State
whether sources are independent. Do not assume timestamps align across edits.

## Open questions and review queue

List missing evidence, attribution uncertainties, timing/wording issues,
contradictions, and the exact check needed to resolve each. Link the day review
queue when it exists. Include an owner/date only if explicitly stated.

## Review and synthesis handoff

Record consequential corrections with source intervals, checks actually run,
remaining limitations, and privacy review. Identify which evidence-backed items
can feed day-level synthesis and which remain provisional. Do not turn an
unperformed check into a pass or hide an earlier conclusion that later changed.
